headline: A Southeast Asian conglomerate still awaits one approval for Altura's $3-million raise
dek: Altura Energy extended the deadline to close its $3-million helium financing to November 30 while its investor's bank sign-off is pending.
caption: A private placement tied to Altura Energy's helium project in Arizona is awaiting one last regulatory sign-off.

sources.title: Altura Energy Provides Further Update on $3 Million Strategic Investment to Expand Helium Production in Arizona

unverified_claims: That the private placement investor is 'a leading Southeast Asian conglomerate' rests solely on Altura's own description; the investor is not named.
That the investor will have the right to nominate one member to the board of directors upon completion is stated only in Altura's release.
brief: Altura Energy Corp. (TSXV: ALTU) has extended the deadline to complete a $3-million non-brokered private placement to November 30, 2026, after the TSX Venture Exchange granted conditional acceptance of the financing. The helium explorer first disclosed the offering in a July 28, 2026 news release.

The offering consists of 18,541,400 units at $0.1618 each, with each unit made up of one common share and one warrant exercisable at $0.25 for 36 months. The investor, described by Altura only as a leading Southeast Asian conglomerate, has its Ministry of Finance's approval but is still waiting on its state bank before it can close.

Altura's release did not name the investor, which it described only as a leading Southeast Asian conglomerate that will have the right to nominate one member to the board of directors once the deal closes. No closing date beyond the November 30 deadline was given.
body: Altura Energy Corp. (TSXV: ALTU) said October 30 that it has extended, to November 30, 2026, the deadline to complete a non-brokered private placement of 18,541,400 units at $0.1618 each, for gross proceeds of C$3 million. The TSX Venture Exchange has granted conditional acceptance of the offering, which the company first disclosed in a July 28, 2026 news release.

Each unit under the offering comprises one common share and one share purchase warrant, exercisable at $0.25 for 36 months from the closing date. A non-brokered placement is one an issuer sells directly to subscribers rather than through an investment dealer, which is consistent with the release naming no agent or underwriter on the transaction.

The sole subscriber is described in the release only as a leading Southeast Asian conglomerate; Altura's release does not name the investor. That investor has obtained approval from its own local Ministry of Finance to proceed, but the release said it is still awaiting a further approval from its state bank before the financing can close.

Altura said the investor will have the right to nominate one member to the board of directors once the placement completes; the release did not disclose who might be nominated or any further governance terms attached to the investment beyond that right.

The extension is the only change disclosed in the October 30 release; the unit count, the per-unit price and the warrant terms are unchanged from the July 28 announcement, according to the company. No new closing date beyond November 30, 2026, was given, and the release did not say what happens if that date passes without the state bank's approval.

Altura describes itself as a helium-focused exploration company advancing prospects in the Holbrook Basin of Arizona, targeting helium for uses the company lists as healthcare, semiconductors, aerospace and other advanced-technology applications. The company also trades on the OTCQB under the symbol ALTUF and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under Y020.
